sections.title: The Vision of the Ram and the Goat
observations: Daniel has a vision of a ram with two horns, representing the Medo-Persian Empire, which is powerful and dominant.
The goat, representing Greece, comes from the west and attacks the ram, symbolizing the conquests of Alexander the Great.
The notable horn on the goat represents Alexander himself, who swiftly conquers the Persian Empire.

sections.title: The Little Horn and Its Blasphemies
observations: From one of the four horns that arise after the notable horn is broken, a little horn emerges, which represents a future king who will be arrogant and blasphemous.
This little horn will persecute the saints and disrupt the daily sacrifices, indicating a time of great tribulation for God's people.

importantVerses.commentary: The little horn that grows exceedingly great, representing a powerful and blasphemous ruler.
The prophecy of 2300 evenings and mornings, indicating a period of oppression and the eventual restoration of the sanctuary.

questions: What does the vision of the ram and goat reveal about God's sovereignty over earthly kingdoms?
How does the rise of the little horn reflect the challenges faced by believers throughout history?
What is the significance of the 2300 evenings and mornings in the context of the prophecy?
